forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

summary.summary: Covering report presenting Tandridge's draft Annual Governance Statement for 2025/26 — the annual self-assessment of governance that must be published alongside the accounts. The statutory officers (Monitoring Officer and S151) state their opinion that the council's overall governance arrangements are sound, and the first draft AGS was published on the council's website before the 30 June 2026 statutory deadline, with the final version due back to committee in autumn 2026 once external audit findings are known. The AGS itself and its 2026/27 action plan sit in appendices not included in this paper, which contains no financial figures.

news_drafts.headline: Tandridge's 2025/26 draft accounts met 30 June deadline; council due to be abolished 31 March 2027
news_drafts.lead:
Tandridge District Council's finance team published its 2025/26 draft accounts on the statutory deadline of 30 June 2026, months before the council is due to be abolished on 31 March 2027, the Audit & Scrutiny Committee's papers show. The papers call it "a fantastic achievement" for a small team that also handled Local Government Reorganisation and took over external audit arrangements (the independent check on the accounts) from Surrey County Council in April 2025. They note that many larger councils missed the deadline.

The 2024/25 accounts were signed off by auditors within statutory deadlines, the council's first full-scale audit since the pre-Covid year of 2018/19. For 2025/26, however, Grant Thornton, the external auditors, expects to issue a disclaimer, meaning it will not give an opinion on the accounts. The paper says the auditors have no assurance over balances brought forward from 2023/24, which were deprioritised in that year's audit. That leaves them unable to vouch for the movements in the year or the prior-year comparisons.

The council's replies to the auditors show how abolition is shaping its plans. Asked to find further recurring savings for its medium-term financial strategy (its multi-year spending plan), the council said its focus is on "financial sustainability to vesting day", the date functions pass to the successor East Surrey authority. It will deliver approved savings "where practicable", maintain reserves and avoid unnecessary pressures for the successor. On housing, it is engaging with the Regulator of Social Housing and developing an improvement plan after a C4 consumer standards grading.

The internal audit progress report lists seven overdue management actions. The business continuity audit of October 2025 gave "No" assurance, the lowest rating, after finding none of eight completed plans had been tested. Its high-priority action, due 30 April 2026, now has a revised date of "TBC". Others date back to a June 2024 asset management audit, where two low-priority actions are now due 30 October 2026.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix A - External Auditors Update October 2026

findings.paper_title: TDC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 Sept 26
findings.headline: Seven management actions across multiple audits are now overdue, extending period before control improvements take effect
findings.detail: In addition to Business Continuity's overdue high-priority action, Annex 2 lists 6 further overdue management actions: two low-priority and one further medium-priority action from Asset Management (Statutory Checks); one medium-priority from Procurement (July 2025); and three from Homelessness (Feb 2026) — one low and two medium priority. The oldest originally due 30 September 2024.
findings.matters: Overdue management actions indicate audit findings are not being remediated on schedule, extending the period that identified control weaknesses persist in the system.
findings.quote: Annex 2 lists under 'Overdue Low & Medium Priority Management Actions': Asset Management (Statutory Checks) 1 Low due 30.09.24 rescheduled 30.10.26; Procurement 1 Medium due 30.09.25 rescheduled 30.09.26; Homelessness with actions rescheduled to 31.10.26

findings.paper_title: TDC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 Sept 26
findings.headline: Asset Management (Statutory Checks) audit from June 2024 with No opinion still has management actions overdue after multiple reschedulings
findings.detail: June 2024 audit issued 'No' assurance opinion and identified 21 management actions (4 low, 9 medium, 8 high priority). Two low-priority actions have become overdue; one originally due 30 September 2024 has been rescheduled four times and is now due 30 October 2026; another was rescheduled from 31 March 2025 through 31 December 2025 and 31 March 2026 to 30 October 2026.
findings.matters: A No-opinion audit from over 18 months ago indicates serious control weaknesses. Multiple reschedulings of remediation suggest either systemic obstacles to implementing improvements or slippage in management attention to control deficiencies.
findings.figures: 21 management actions agreed June 2024; 2 low-priority actions now overdue with revised due date October 2026
findings.quote: Asset Management (Statutory Checks) 25.06.24 ... No 4 9 8 ... [with overdue low-priority actions dated 30.09.24 rescheduled to 30.10.26 and 31.03.25 rescheduled to 30.10.26]

findings.paper_title: TDC Internal Audit Progress Report 2026-27 Sept 26
findings.headline: Business Continuity audit (No opinion) has overdue high-priority management action with revised completion date marked TBC
findings.detail: October 2025 audit gave 'No' assurance opinion (the lowest rating) after finding that none of eight completed business continuity plans had been tested and lessons learned incorporated. High-priority management action to test plans, originally due 30 April 2026, now has revised completion date of TBC. Audit also found no specific BCP training or guidance available to officers with listed responsibilities.
findings.matters: Business continuity is fundamental operational risk; untested plans mean the council cannot assure it can respond to disruption. Unclear remediation timeline is concerning.
findings.figures: Original due date 30 April 2026; revised to TBC. Eight BCPs drafted, none tested.
findings.quote: No deadline has been set by EMT to ensure that BCP's are tested and across the eight completed BCPs no testing has been scheduled within 2025/26.

findings.headline: 2025/26 draft statutory accounts published on statutory deadline of 30 June 2026 by small finance team
findings.detail: The council's finance team published 2025/26 draft accounts on 30 June 2026, meeting the statutory deadline. This achievement occurred while managing a small team size, Local Government Reorganisation pressures, and the April 2025 transition to in-house external audit delivery. The paper notes that many councils with significantly larger resource pools did not meet this deadline.
findings.matters: Timely publication of draft statutory accounts is a statutory requirement; achieving it under resource and organisational constraints demonstrates effective financial control, and is relevant to peer councils in similar situations.
findings.quote: The Councils Finance team completed and published the 2025/26 draft statutory accounts by the statutory deadline 30th June 2026, which must be acknowledge as a fantastic achievement.

findings.headline: 2024/25 accounts completed and signed off by auditors within statutory deadlines, first full-scale audit since pre-Covid 2018/19
findings.detail: The 2024/25 accounts were completed and signed off by auditors within statutory deadlines, representing the council's first full-scale audit cycle since pre-Covid 2018/19. This was achieved despite the council taking on external audit delivery from Surrey County Council from April 2025 and managing concurrent pressures from Local Government Reorganisation.
findings.matters: Completion of a full audit cycle on time after years of Covid-related audit backlog signals return to normal financial reporting capability; lenders and peer councils track this as evidence of audit recovery progress.
findings.quote: 2024/25 was the first full scale statutory audit the Council's worked through, since the pre -covid year 2018/19

daily_post.headline: Homelessness and temporary accommodation costs are highly volatile and present a material downside risk to budget
daily_post.lead: Temporary accommodation is a high-volatility cost line and the council's own commentary shows it lacks full control over the exposure; significant growth could force reserve drawdowns or service cuts.
